sections.title: Identification and habit
sections.text: The catalogue entry Daucus describes Daucus carota, wild carrot, rather than the whole genus. This biennial reaches about 0.6–1.2 m when flowering. Its leaves are finely divided and its small white flowers form umbels often surrounded by divided bracts.

sections.title: Root and caution
sections.text: The enlarged root of cultivated forms of D. carota is eaten; the plate chiefly shows the flowering plant and umbels, not a table carrot root. The umbels can be confused with those of highly poisonous Apiaceae, including water hemlock: do not gather a plant based on an illustration alone.
